Projects.name: Cloud Resume Challenge
details: Architected and continue to operate a serverless full-stack platform spanning 15+ AWS services — CloudFront, WAF, API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB, S3, SES, SQS, EventBridge, KMS, and Route 53 — codified end to end as least-privilege Terraform across frontend, backend, IAM, and repository modules, with every change peer-reviewed via plan output on pull requests.

Replaced a hand-maintained PDF with a CV compiled on demand from the site's own data: a Lambda renders an ATS-friendly PDF through a hand-written, dependency-free PDF writer, caches it in S3 under a content digest so it only re-renders when the CV's content changes, and serves it via per-click 60-second signed CloudFront URLs from a hand-rolled RSA-SHA1 signer.

Kept the real inbox off the freely downloadable CV with a disposable forwarding address: each CV prints a monthly-rotating alias on the site's domain, and inbound SES mail feeds a Lambda that drops spam, malware, spoofed, and revoked-alias mail, relays the rest with Reply-To set to the sender, and raises abuse alerts.

Designed a single GitHub Actions pipeline that gates every pull request on unit tests, typechecking, a Cypress end-to-end run, and a Terraform plan, then skips re-verifying unchanged code on merge via content-digest markers while still smoke-testing production after every deploy and infrastructure apply.

Hardened the contact form with fail-closed, server-side reCAPTCHA verification and CloudWatch alarms that email an SNS alert on any failed submission; kept the CloudFront signing key and reCAPTCHA secret out of Terraform state by reading them from SSM Parameter Store at runtime, and the real inbox out of the public repository and its published plan logs via a secret-fed sensitive variable.

Projects.name: SwiftX
details: Ported a comprehensive screenshot and file-sharing application from C# to native Swift, achieving full feature parity with upstream releases while leveraging macOS APIs (AppKit, CoreGraphics, AVFoundation) for optimal performance and system integration.

Implemented 50+ automation features including custom hotkeys, drag-and-drop upload, cloud service integrations, and post-capture tasks (annotation, compression, URL shortening), enabling power users to streamline content-sharing workflows and reduce manual steps by up to 80%.

Engineered robust screen capture and video recording systems supporting multiple output formats, real-time frame capture via Metal rendering, and configurable quality settings, enabling creators to rapidly produce and share multimedia content.

Integrated 20+ cloud storage and sharing services (AWS S3, Google Drive, Imgur, and more) with credential management and OAuth authentication, providing flexible deployment options and reducing lock-in to proprietary solutions.

Designed a modular Swift codebase with clear separation of concerns, async/await patterns, and type-safe APIs, reducing maintenance burden while improving reliability and enabling rapid iteration on new features.

Projects.name: Animatic
details: Building a native Rust successor to AniDB O'Matic, a Windows anime-library manager, for Windows and Linux: an egui desktop app over a SQLite library that hashes local media in a single pass (ED2K, CRC32, MD5, SHA-1), identifies files against AniDB, and keeps the user's MyList in sync.

Designed a durable, offline-first synchronization queue that coalesces repeated edits to the latest intent, retains failures for review, and persists cooldowns across restarts, with AniDB's UDP and HTTP request spacing and once-a-day limits enforced program-wide and saved before every request, so a restart never resets them.

Implemented a read-only importer for the legacy application's encrypted databanks that never modifies the originals, a reviewable migration of its settings, and a compatible implementation of its file-renaming expression language with diagnostics, preview, and explicit confirmation.

Split the codebase into three crates (a storage-free AniDB protocol client, a core library, and the desktop app) covered by more than 600 Rust tests, with credentials kept in the operating-system keystore, validated library backup and restore, and explicit, checksum-verified in-app updates from GitHub releases.

Projects.name: Japan Immigration Statistics Dashboard
details: Originally built the dashboard on Create React App and attracted over 2,000 unique users in its first 30 days, then, after CRA's deprecation, carried it through a ground-up 'Civic Glass' redesign onto Next.js 15, React 19, and strict TypeScript, replacing Chart.js with a vendored visx-based chart library.

Expanded the dashboard from 4 to 7 interactive chart types, including two charts hand-built without a charting library — a zoomable category-mix treemap and a ranked processing-efficiency lollipop chart — alongside a Sankey outcomes flow with an approval-rate gauge and an interactive prefectural choropleth map.
Developed a processing time estimator using historical trends and 3-month rolling averages to forecast queue positions and completion dates, helping applicants plan around uncertain timelines.

Automated data freshness with a daily GitHub Actions watcher that polls Japan's e-Stat API, diffs each release's survey date against the last run, and triggers a build only when new or corrected statistics are published, so most daily runs publish nothing.

Built a build-time data transform that deaggregates regional bureau statistics so branch offices like Narita and Kansai airports stop being double-counted in their parent bureau's totals, while shrinking the client-side data payload by roughly 10x.

Shipped a localisation foundation where every string, number format, and pluralisation rule is sourced from one catalogue file per language, with a build-time check that fails if a language marked complete is missing a string added since.

Projects.name: Handoff for Slate
details: Designed and shipped a commercial Unreal Engine 5.7/5.8 editor plugin on Fab that generates readable Slate C++ from Figma designs, one SCompoundWidget class per screen and component plus a style class, depending only on Slate and SlateCore, and re-imports design revisions as a line-level three-way merge so hand-written code survives every design change.

Applied the generation-gap pattern so each class is split into regenerated Generated/S<Name>Base files owned by the tool and S<Name> files owned by the developer, written once and never touched again, with deterministic output so the same package always produces the same files, in the same order, with the same names.

Built the merge around per-file baselines of what the last import generated: design-only changes apply, hand edits inside generated files are kept, and overlapping changes surface as conflicts in a reviewable diff window that defaults to keeping the developer's lines; members referenced by the developer's code are never removed or silently retyped.

Shared the package format, companion Figma exporter, identity and re-link matching, and safety net with Handoff for UMG, and added a pre-compile preview that builds the screens with live widgets, a Python API, a CI commandlet with exit codes, and 16 setup health checks that verify module dependencies and packaging.

Projects.name: Handoff for UMG
details: Designed and shipped a commercial Unreal Engine 5.7/5.8 editor plugin on Fab that turns Figma designs into ordinary UMG Widget Blueprints and re-imports later design revisions as a per-property three-way merge, so the Blueprint graphs, bindings, and hand edits built on top of an import survive every design change.

Built the re-import planner around a deterministic manifest of per-property hashes (last design value, value written, accepted local edit): design-only changes apply, Unreal-only edits are kept, and changes on both sides surface as conflicts in a reviewable diff window that defaults to keeping the Unreal edit; re-importing an unchanged package plans zero changes.

Engineered stable widget identity with frozen names derived from an FNV-1a hash of each design node id and deterministic widget GUIDs, plus a weighted fallback matcher (hierarchy path, layer name, type, geometry) that re-links copy-pasted or re-identified frames automatically only above a strict threshold and offers weaker matches as suggestions.

Protected projects with a safety net that backs up affected assets and the manifest before every apply and restores them byte for byte, locks widgets referenced by graphs, bindings, animations, or BindWidget members against removal, and checks files out of source control when needed.

Shipped a free companion Figma exporter and a documented, tool-neutral package format, an optional CommonUI mode generating text and button styles, CommonButtonBase buttons, and CommonActivatableWidget screens, and automation through a Python API, a CI commandlet with exit codes, 16 built-in setup health checks, and one-click support bundles.

Projects.name: Keystone Prefabs
details: Designed and shipped a commercial Unreal Engine 5.7/5.8 editor plugin on Fab that brings a Unity-style prefab workflow to Unreal, with nested prefabs and cycle detection, variants that store only their differences from a parent, and in-place Edit/Commit/Discard that updates every loaded instance in a single undoable transaction.

Built a per-instance override system that tracks property and node-transform changes automatically and surfaces Revert to Prefab and Apply to Prefab controls directly in the Details panel, with Apply able to target the prefab itself, a variant parent, or a nested prefab.

Engineered World Partition support by keeping each prefab instance as a single actor with component nodes, so one instance is one external actor file; stale instances in unloaded cells are found through actor descriptors without loading them, and re-synced in bulk by a commandlet with dry-run, CI verify, and source-control checkout modes.

Added a Pack step that collapses identical static meshes into ISM/HISM components with a before-and-after draw-call estimate, taking a 1,000-mesh prefab from 1,000 estimated draw calls to 1, and a Bake step that exports to plain actors, Level Instances, or Packed Level Actors so users are never locked in.

Exposed a Python API for batch work and runtime spawning from cooked data for Blueprint and C++, backed by 21 Python editor tests, 6 editor UI automation tests, and a packaged Win64 smoke test, and published user documentation with a built-in diagnostics report wired into the GitHub issue templates.

Projects.name: Interactive Switches
details: Designed and developed a configurable lighting-control system for Unreal Engine in which switch plates of up to four switches can each be wired to any number of lights, including lights of different component types, just like real-world switches.

Shipped v2.0 with full server-authoritative network replication: light state is a RepNotify variable written only on the server, so every client, including players who join late, sees the same lights and switch positions across Listen Server, Dedicated Server, and standalone play.

Kept networking lightweight by routing player interaction through a single reliable Server RPC, leaving switches as non-replicated actors that animate locally from their lights' replicated state, and placing idle lights in network dormancy so they use no bandwidth until they change.

Built the system entirely in Blueprints around a parent light class and master switch Blueprints, so developers add new light types as child classes and hook cosmetic changes into a state-change event without touching the switch logic.

Supported every Unreal Engine release from 4.20 through 5.8, publishing v2.0 for UE 5.8 alongside the single-player v1.0 for earlier engines, with polished switch meshes, materials, and a post-process interaction outline included.
